summary:
Background

Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

Methods

In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116.

Findings

Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group.

Interpretation

In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

summary:
Background

Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

Methods

In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. The data cutoff date was March 23, 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival were evaluated as dual primary endpoints using a graphical multiple-testing approach with prespecified alpha allocation. Progression-free survival was assessed every 8 weeks through to week 56, then every 12 weeks thereafter; overall survival was assessed continuously. The safety analysis included all randomly assigned patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. For progression-free survival, missing radiographic assessments were handled using prespecified censoring rules; no imputation was performed for missing overall survival or safety data. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06132958) and is ongoing.

Findings

Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p<0·0001) and median overall survival was 19·0 months (16·1-not reached) in the sac-TMT group and 12·1 months (11·0-15·2) in the TPC group (0·68 [0·55-0·84]; p=0·0001). 265 (69%) of 384 patients in the sac-TMT group and 210 (57%) of 367 in the TPC group had a grade 3 or higher adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 133 (35%) patients in the sac-TMT group and 117 (32%) patients in the TPC group. Treatment-related adverse events led to death in three (<1%) patients in the sac-TMT group and three (<1%) in the TPC group.

Interpretation

Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

Merck Sharp & Dohme.

summary:
Background

Patients with heavily pretreated hormone receptor-positive and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer have few treatment options. Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class, epidermal growth factor receptor and HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate that contains a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (Ed-04). The aim of PANKU-Breast01 was to compare the efficacy and safety of iza-bren versus chemotherapy in patients with pretreated HR+/HER2- breast cancer.

Methods

In this randomised, phase 3, open-label, multicentre study in 72 hospitals in China, patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer who had disease progression after endocrine therapy, cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg, administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks) or physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, 1·4 mg/m2; vinorelbine, 25 mg/m2; or gemcitabine, 1000 mg/m2, all administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks; or capecitabine, 1000-1250 mg/m2, administered orally twice daily on days 1-14 of each 3-week cycle). Stratified block randomisation was performed by an independent vendor using an interactive web response system, with stratification factors of number of previous lines of chemotherapy, CNS metastasis, and HER2 expression status. Patients, investigators, and site personnel involved in patient care and performing trial procedures were not masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review per RECIST (version 1.1) in the modified intention-to-treat population, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who had at least one dose of study drug. Median progression-free survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06343948, and is closed to recruitment.

Findings

Between April 24, 2024, and June 6, 2025, 560 patients were screened, 177 were excluded, and 383 patients were randomly assigned and treated (190 were assigned to the iza-bren group and 193 were assigned to the chemotherapy group). All 383 participants in the study were female and of Chinese ethnicity. Median age was 54·0 years (IQR 47·0-60·0). At data cutoff (July 21, 2026), median follow-up for progression-free survival was 15·2 months (95% CI 13·9-16·8). Iza-bren significantly improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy (log-rank p<0·0001), and median progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review was 8·2 months (95% CI 6·9-8·6) versus 4·0 months (2·9-4·3; HR 0·41 [95% CI 0·33-0·53]). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 162 (85%) patients in the iza-bren group versus 127 (66%) patients in the chemotherapy group, and haematological adverse events were the most common in both groups. For the treatment of haematological adverse events, 138 (73%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet-elevating agents, 28 (15%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet transfusion, and 18 patients (10%) in the iza-bren group received a blood transfusion. Two patients in the iza-bren group died due to treatment-related adverse events.

Interpretation

Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

summary:
Background

A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.

Methods

The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.

Findings

Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).

Interpretation

First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

summary:
Background

Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.

Methods

HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing.

Findings

Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related.

Interpretation

Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting.

Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

summary:
Background

Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.

Methods

PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.

Findings

Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.

Interpretation

A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

summary:
Background

Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.

Methods

REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.

Findings

Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). Background

Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.

Methods

This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.

Findings

Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.

Interpretation

The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

summary:
Background

Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival.

Methods

In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual.

Findings

From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative.

Interpretation

In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.

title: Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial.

summary: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis-a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. Despite its burden and costs, osteoarthritis remains largely invisible in national and global health agendas, is poorly integrated within service models for other chronic health conditions, and is frequently perceived as inevitable with ageing and associated with limited therapeutic options. This context drives an osteoarthritis identity problem that fuels frustration among those living with the disease and health-care professionals, perpetuates stigma and inequities, undermines access to effective interventions, and crucially, deprioritises osteoarthritis in health policy. How can health systems be strengthened to mitigate the burden of disease and prioritise the prevention and control of osteoarthritis? We outline a co-created, globally relevant roadmap for health policy responses for osteoarthritis prevention and care that extend beyond the UN's Agenda 2030 targets. The intended audience for the roadmap includes health policy makers, health services managers, clinicians, and civil society organisations. The roadmap anchors to three strategic priorities underpinned by guiding principles of a life course approach, prioritising health equity, and ensuring that responses are affordable and sustainable across economies. Priority 1: recognise and respond to osteoarthritis with capacity building in national surveillance of burden, cost, and modifiable risk factors, and explicitly embedding musculoskeletal health within national and subnational health policies. Priority 2: scale up high-value, person-centred, equitable care for approximately 600 million people living with osteoarthritis. This priority requires reframing of societal narratives around osteoarthritis and reconfiguring service models to integrate osteoarthritis into primary and chronic disease care while also addressing social, environmental, and commercial determinants of musculoskeletal health. Priority 3: slow the osteoarthritis trajectory via primary and secondary prevention targeted at excess bodyweight and joint injury, enabled by cross-sectoral and cross-disease cooperation. These priorities are supported by accelerators requiring global collaboration, within and outside the osteoarthritis community.
title: Strengthening health systems to prioritise, provide care, and prevent osteoarthritis: a roadmap for global health policy.

summary: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. Insofar as we protect the planet or invest in fruitful research on pandemic countermeasures, we promote future wellbeing and health, sometimes at the present generation's expense. As we warm the planet, accelerate antibiotic resistance, or consume finite natural resources, we might serve present-day wellbeing or health at the expense of future generations. To decide which such trade-offs are legitimate or advisable, we need to know how to balance the health interests of future generations against each other and against our own. Should concerns for future health be confined to the 21st century as per the stated mission of the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health? If not, how far into the future should they extend, and why? Population ethics is a branch of ethics that considers future populations' wellbeing. This Review, a part of the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health, applies general insights from population ethics to future populations' health, and shows why that application is more complex than meets the eye.
title: Addressing threats to future global health-what is the right timeframe?

Background

Artificial intelligence (AI)-based systems show promise for assisting primary care providers (PCPs) with patient care. We aimed to evaluate the safety and quality of clinical conversations of a patient-facing conversational AI system, which engaged in real-world urgent primary care appointments.

Methods

In this prospective, single-centre, single-arm feasibility study, English-speaking patients aged at least 18 years interacted with the Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer (AMIE) up to 5 days before a single-complaint urgent primary care appointment. Physician safety supervisors monitored all interactions and were trained to intervene on the basis of predefined safety criteria. AMIE transcripts and summaries were shared with PCPs before the visit. Primary outcomes were the number of supervised conversation safety stops, AMIE's conversation quality assessed by clinical evaluators, and patient and PCP experiences per surveys. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06911398).

Findings

From April to November, 2025, 114 patients were enrolled with 98 completing both the AMIE interaction and the PCP appointment. Zero conversation safety stops were required on the basis of prespecified criteria. Safety supervisors noted one hallucination and added clinical information in five interactions. AMIE's conversations were rated favourably in 87-100% of cases (17 criteria) by clinical evaluators, and 48-96% (16 criteria) by patients. Patient attitudes towards AI improved after interacting with AMIE and remained elevated after the patient's visit with their physician. PCPs completed post-surveys in 60 of 98 cases, including 44 cases in which they reviewed the AMIE transcript before the visit. PCPs found AMIE helpful for visit preparation in 33 of 44 cases and reported that it might have changed their behaviour in 25 of 44 cases.

Interpretation

Although further research is needed, this study shows the initial feasibility of conversational AI in a real-world setting-assessed via conversation safety and quality, as well as user acceptance-and represents a crucial step towards clinical translation.

summary:
Background

In hereditary angioedema, a rare bradykinin-mediated condition, oral on-demand treatments facilitating prompt administration and providing rapid, sustained relief and attack resolution remain scant. We investigated the efficacy and safety of deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks.

Methods

RAPIDe-3 was a phase 3, double-blind, 2 × 2 crossover trial in adolescent and adult participants (aged ≥12 to <18 years and aged ≥18 to ≤75 years, respectively) with hereditary angioedema, at 59 sites across 24 countries on six continents. Eligible participants had hereditary angioedema, including those with normal C1 inhibitor associated with a documented genetic variant, at least two attacks within the last 3 months before screening, and experience with effectively using conventional on-demand therapies for hereditary angioedema attacks. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two double-blind crossover sequences to treat two attacks with a 20 mg oral deucrictibant immediate-release capsule or placebo as either deucrictibant-placebo or placebo-deucrictibant, stratified by age and use of long-term prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was time to onset of symptom relief, defined as Patient Global Impression of Change rating of at least a little better. Safety was assessed in all participants who received any dose of study drug. RAPIDe-3 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06343779) and is complete.

Findings

Between April 4, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, 149 people were assessed for eligibility, and 134 eligible participants (ten [7%] adolescents and 124 [93%] adults) were randomly allocated. 58 (43%) were male and 76 (57%) were female, and the median age was 38·0 years (IQR 27·0-50·0). 113 participants treated 201 attacks. The primary efficacy analysis included 88 participants with paired treated attacks. Of these, 47 (53%) participants were female and 41 (47%) were male, and 60 (68%), 16 (18%), 4 (5%), and 1 (1%) were White, Asian, Black, and American Indian or Alaska Native, respectively. Onset of symptom relief occurred significantly faster with deucrictibant than placebo, with median times of 1·28 h (95% CI 1·05 to 1·52) and more than 12 h (5·82 to >12), respectively (p<0·0001). Fatigue was the only adverse event reported more than once within 3 days post-treatment: a single event was reported by two participants, one of which was deemed unrelated to treatment. Across the study, no treatment-related adverse events were assessed as severe or serious, and no adverse events led to treatment discontinuation.

Interpretation

Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration.

summary: Migraine is a chronic neurovascular disorder characterised by recurrent attacks of moderate-to-severe head pain, accompanied by transient but disabling symptoms such as aura, nausea, vomiting, phonophobia, and photophobia, reflecting the involvement of multiple systems. Migraine affects and disables a large proportion of the global population. The pathogenesis of migraine involves the interplay of genetic and epigenetic factors across complex neurosensory and neurovascular networks. Decades of research have elucidated key components of these pathways, driving the development of mechanism-based therapies that are now transforming clinical practice and substantially improving patients' lives.
title: Migraine.

summary: Children and adolescents are growing up in a hybrid world in which digital media has become part of the infrastructure of everyday life and a structural determinant of their health. In the second paper of this Series on the digital determinants of health, we apply the framework introduced in the first paper to one of the most contested questions in public health: how young people's digital media use shapes their health and wellbeing. Using the digital determinants of health framework to interpret the current evidence base, we examine what is known, and what remains poorly understood, about the public health implications of children's and adolescents' digital media use. Evidence suggests that digital media use can be associated with both benefits and harms although it is more consistently associated with adverse mental, behavioural, physical, cognitive, and social outcomes, with developmental stage emerging as an important moderator. Illustrative modelling indicates the potential population burden is substantial, even as its causal basis remains uncertain. Research to date has privileged easily measured proxies, such as screen time, and given insufficient attention to the platform design, algorithmic systems, and commercial incentives that shape young people's experiences. Situating young people's digital media use with a digital determinants of health framework, we conclude that protecting children's and adolescents' health calls for a precautionary, structural response-one that moves beyond individual behaviour change to reshape the digital systems, incentives, and knowledge practices that determine how digital media affects health.
title: The public health challenges of children's and adolescents' digital media use: applying the digital determinants of health as an interpretive framework.

authors: Prainsack B, Medhora RP, Kickbusch I.
summary: The digital determinants of health are the structural conditions through which digital infrastructures, business models, and design choices shape health outcomes. Yet these determinants remain largely outside public health policy and remain fragmented across regulatory sectors. Rather than regulating individual technologies in isolation, governance should ensure that digital systems and environments advance population health and reduce inequities. A public health approach shifts attention from individual responsibility-and the tendency to blame users-towards the governance of the structural features that produce health risks and inequities. We identify four governance domains for the digital determinants of health: infrastructure and access, platform design and commercial practices, data governance and surveillance, and institutional accountability and rights. Effectively governing these domains requires intersectoral strategies that tackle problematic concentrations of political and economic power. We argue that the governance of the digital determinants of health should be recognised as a core public health function, with the health of children and young people as a priority and entry point and precaution as a guiding governance principle.
title: Governing the digital determinants of health for children and young people: a global public health imperative.

authors: Shaw J, Gross N, Saldaña-Tejeda A, Atuire C, Prainsack B, Holly L, Kickbusch I.
summary: Digital transformations exert increasing influence over the lives of the global population, shaping opportunities and generating harms for health and wellbeing across the spectrum of digital access and engagement. The scale of influence of digital transformations on human and planetary health marks the urgency of attention to the digital determinants of health (DDoH). In this Series paper, we describe a prevailing digital sociotechnological order (DSTO) as the structural source of the DDoH. The DSTO is composed of a set of dominant assumptions that motivate digital practices operating through four features (political norms, economic logics, infrastructures, and personal and social practices) to affect human and planetary health. We describe the implications of the DSTO for understanding, studying, and governing the DDoH, and present recommendations for future work.
title: The digital determinants of health: a new era for global public health.

Background

Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease.

Methods

We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing.

Findings

A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related.

Interpretation

Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease.

summary:
Background

Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis.

Methods

RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete.

Findings

Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). Further, on intention-to-treat analysis, the proportion of participants reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (414/443; 93·5% [90·9 to 95·5]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (401/437; 91·8% [88·8 to 94·2]) with a risk difference of -1·7% (-5·2 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event.

Interpretation

An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. This finding supports shortening the duration of treatment in such patients.

summary:
Background

Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.

Methods

This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.

Findings

Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.

Interpretation

In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.

authors: Lindland ES, Frascheri-Verzelli L, Ljøstad U.
summary: In this Clinical Rounds, we present a case of neuroborreliosis in a man aged 59 years who initially complained of headache, tremor, and hiccups. Diagnosis was delayed, partly due to an atypical presentation but mainly because subtle MRI findings were overlooked. There is emerging recognition that radial and patchy hyperintensities in cerebral peduncles, mesencephalon, and pons is a distinct MRI feature of neuroborreliosis. Dissemination of this knowledge could contribute to more timely and efficient diagnoses in future patients.
title: A trembling detour to the diagnosis of encephalitis: a neuroborreliosis case report.

authors: Bellido V, le Roux CW, Ekinci EI, Bjornstad P, Frias JP, Giblin K, Eyde S, Park SY, Ferro J, Johnson C, Taylor A.
summary:
Background

Retatrutide is an agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, and is currently under investigation for the treatment of obesity, type 2 diabetes, and other comorbidities, including knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnoea. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

Methods

TRIUMPH-2 was a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 92 medical and research centres and hospitals across eight countries. We enrolled adults (aged ≥18 years) with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or higher and type 2 diabetes (glycated haemoglobin [HbA1c] 6·5-10·5%) on stable treatment for type 2 diabetes for at least 90 days before screening (diet or exercise alone, or up to three oral glucose-lowering medications), and a history of at least one self-reported unsuccessful dietary effort to reduce bodyweight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1), using an interactive web-response system, to receive once-weekly subcutaneous injections (self-administered) of placebo or retatrutide 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg. The primary endpoint was the percentage change from baseline to week 80 in bodyweight for the retatrutide 9 mg and 12 mg doses versus placebo, with 4 mg versus placebo a key secondary endpoint. Efficacy analyses included all randomly assigned participants, with missing data imputed with a primary multiple imputation strategy for the treatment regimen estimand. Safety analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05929079 (completed).

Findings

Between July 11, 2023, and Nov 1, 2024, 2047 participants were screened, and 1152 (mean age 55·1 years [SD 10·8], 554 [48%] females and 598 [52%] males, and 672 [58%] of White ethnicity) were randomly assigned to retatrutide 4 mg (n=292), 9 mg (n=284), or 12 mg (n=287), or placebo (n=289). At baseline, the mean BMI was 38·2 kg/m2 (SD 7·4), mean HbA1c was 7·71% (1·07), median duration of obesity was 21 years (IQR 11-31), and median duration of diabetes was 5·6 years (2·6-10·4). At baseline, 1055 (92%) of 1152 participants were on any oral glucose-lowering medication, including biguanides, SGLT2 inhibitors, sulfonylureas, and other oral glucose-lowering medications. Of 1152 participants, 965 (84%) completed the study drug. For the treatment regimen estimand, the mean percentage change from baseline in bodyweight at week 80 was -11·9% (SE 0·6) with retatrutide 4 mg, -16·8% (0·7) with retatrutide 9 mg, -18·8% (0·7) with retatrutide 12 mg, and -5·1% (0·7) with placebo. Estimated treatment differences compared with placebo for percentage change in bodyweight were -6·9% (95% CI -8·7 to -5·1) with retatrutide 4 mg, -11·8% (-13·7 to -9·8) with retatrutide 9 mg, and -13·8% (-15·8 to -11·8) with retatrutide 12 mg (p<0·0001 for all). The most frequently reported adverse events were gastrointestinal, which were more common in the retatrutide groups than in the placebo group (diarrhoea occurred in 80 [27%] of 292 participants in the 4 mg group, 95 [34%] of 284 in the 9 mg group, and 96 [34%] of 286 in the 12 mg group vs 38 [13%] of 287 in the placebo group, and nausea occurred in 40 [14%], 59 [21%], and 80 [28%] vs 23 [8%]). Hypotension and dysesthesia were more frequent with retatrutide than with placebo (four [1%] in the 4 mg group, 14 [5%] in the 9 mg group, and 18 (6%) in the 12 mg group vs one [<1%] in the placebo group with hypotension; 13 [4%], 16 [6%], and 21 [7%] vs two [1%] in the placebo group with dysesthesia). Permanent treatment discontinuation due to adverse events or death was more frequent in participants treated with retatrutide 9 mg (33 [12%]) and 12 mg (22 [8%]) compared with retatrutide 4 mg (11 [4%]) and placebo (14 [5%]). Two participants died in the retatrutide 4 mg group, three in the 9 mg group, one in the 12 mg group, and one in the placebo group; all deaths were deemed to be unrelated to the study intervention by the investigator.

Interpretation

Treatment with retatrutide resulted in substantial improvements in bodyweight and was associated with improvements in glycaemic control in participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes, with a safety profile generally consistent with other molecules with GLP-1 receptor agonism. These results show that retatrutide might be effective for the treatment of obesity in people with type 2 diabetes.

Funding

Eli Lilly and Company.
title: Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2): a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

authors: Papa R, Rhee S, Delai P, Zhang K, Balcázar IB, Rethanavelu K, Fujiwara T, Mishima K, Tabarkiewicz J, Funck-Brentano T, Stander R, Bachiller-Corral J, Dahir KM, Eekhoff EMW, Hero M, Kuong E, Uemura N, Zhou M, Trotter DG, Gu J, Sanchez RJ, O'Donovan DÓ, Economides AN, Pordy R, Hirshberg B, Yancopoulos GD, Keen R, OPTIMA Study Group.
summary:
Background

Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare genetic disorder resulting in progressive heterotopic ossification of ligaments, tendons, and muscles, leading to disability and early mortality. FOP is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the activin receptor type 1A, allowing this receptor to be aberrantly activated by activin A (ActA), which normally inhibits this receptor, thus driving heterotopic bone formation. In preclinical models and an earlier phase 2 trial (LUMINA-1) in FOP, an antibody blocking ActA (garetosmab) prevented heterotopic ossification. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of garetosmab in adults living with FOP.

Methods

OPTIMA is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 18 study sites across 16 countries and regions. Participants aged 18 years or older with FOP were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to monthly intravenous placebo, garetosmab 3 mg/kg, or garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Randomisation was stratified by baseline Cumulative Analogue Joint Involvement Scale score and previous participation in the LUMINA-1 study. The primary efficacy and safety endpoints were total number of new heterotopic bone lesions at week 56 and treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs) through week 56, analysed in all randomised participants who received at least one dose of the study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05394116); the trial is active (completed primary endpoint) but not recruiting participants.

Findings

Between Nov 21, 2022, and July 4, 2024, 63 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned (placebo, n=21; garetosmab 3 mg/kg, n=19; garetosmab 10 mg/kg, n=23). The mean age was 26·6 years (SD 6·8); 38 (60%) participants were female and 25 (40%) male. 62 participants completed 56 weeks of treatment; one participant in the placebo group discontinued at 53 weeks. The total number of new heterotopic bone lesions was significantly lower with garetosmab: there were 19 lesions with placebo versus one lesion with garetosmab 3 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·06 [95% CI 0·00-0·73]; p=0·027) and two lesions with garetosmab 10 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·10 [0·01-0·76]; p=0·026). Treatment-emergent AESIs occurred in one (5%) of 21 participants receiving placebo, zero of 19 receiving garetosmab 3 mg/kg, and four (17%) of 23 receiving garetosmab 10 mg/kg; all were considered treatment-related. No deaths occurred.

Interpretation

Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.

Funding

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.
title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

summary:
Background

WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma is a primary brain tumour with a high risk of recurrence even after complete surgical resection. The role of adjuvant radiotherapy remains uncertain. We aimed to assess whether adjuvant radiotherapy reduces recurrence compared with observation in patients with a newly diagnosed atypical meningioma who have undergone complete surgical resection.

Methods

ROAM/EORTC-1308 was an international, multicentre, open-label, phase 3, randomised controlled trial, conducted at 58 hospitals and academic centres in 11 countries. Eligible sites had appropriate multidisciplinary expertise, neurosurgery, and radiotherapy facilities. Patients aged 16 years or older who had undergone a surgeon-assessed complete surgical resection of newly diagnosed atypical meningioma were randomly assigned (1:1) to adjuvant radiotherapy or observation. Randomisation was done using a web-based interface using random variable blocks of sizes two and four, stratified by location (UK or non-UK). Participants assigned to the radiotherapy group received fractionated external-beam intensity-modulated radiotherapy at a total dose of 60 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks. Participants were followed up for a minimum of 4 years. The primary outcome was disease-free survival, defined as time from surgery to MRI-confirmed recurrence or death due to any cause, analysed in all randomly assigned participants in their assigned treatment group. Harms analysis was done in the as-treated population. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, ISRCTN71502099, and has completed.

Findings

Between April 28, 2016, and May 21, 2021, 990 patients were assessed for eligibility, 157 of whom were randomly assigned to radiotherapy (n=78) or observation (n=79). Median age was 57·40 years (IQR 49·09-66·93); 84 (54%) participants were female and 73 (46%) were male. At a median follow-up of 64 months (IQR 50-75), meningioma recurrence occurred in 11 (14%) of 78 participants in the radiotherapy group and 24 (30%) of 79 in the observation group. 5-year disease-free survival was 79·9% (95% CI 67·6-87·9) in the radiotherapy group and 64·3% (51·9-74·2) in the observation group (absolute difference 15·6% percentage points [95% CI 0·6-30·5]). Disease-free survival was improved in the radiotherapy group compared with the observation group (hazard ratio 0·51 [95% CI 0·27-0·97]; p=0·0396). Grade 2 or 3 radiation-related serious adverse events occurred in five (8%) of 66 participants in the radiotherapy group, with no treatment-related deaths.

Interpretation

Our findings suggest that adjuvant radiotherapy should be considered in patients with atypical meningioma after complete surgical resection of atypical meningioma when the prevention of recurrence is valued higher than the potential delayed adverse effects of radiotherapy. This practice will benefit patients by reducing meningioma recurrence. Decisions should be based on individual discussion with the patient.

Funding

National Institute for Health and Care Research Health Technology Assessment programme, the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Brain Tumour Group and Radiation Oncology Group, and the Heath Research and Medical Research Council of Australia.
title: Radiotherapy versus observation following surgical resection of WHO grade 2 atypical meningioma (ROAM/EORTC-1308): an international, multicentre, open-label, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.

authors: Johnsen PH, Juul FE, Hoff DAL, Hillestad ER, Holme Ø, Skjevling LK, Hansen HM, Rasmus MH, Barnett L, Barry SJE, Hjerde E, Lindstedt K, Buczek DJ, Hatlebakk JG, Steinsvik EK, Berentsen B, Garborg KK, Valeur J, Valle PC, Løberg M, Kalager M, Bretthauer M, Goll R.
summary:
Background

Gut microbiota composition might have a role in the pathogenesis of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and faecal microbiota transplantation has been proposed as a means of restoring healthy gut microbiota for individuals with this condition. We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of faecal microbiota transplantation in patients with IBS.

Methods

In this parallel-group, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, conducted at five hospitals in Norway, we enrolled men and women aged 18-65 years with moderate-to-severe IBS. IBS diagnosis was defined by the Rome IV criteria and an IBS-Severity Scoring System (IBS-SSS) score of 175 points or higher. A colonoscopy within 5 years before study enrolment was required for all participants aged 50 years or older to rule out colorectal cancer, and participants with IBS with predominantly diarrhoea required negative biopsies to exclude microscopic colitis. Participants were randomly assigned 2:1 to faecal microbiota transplantation with faeces samples from either healthy donors (intervention) or the participants themselves (placebo group). All investigators, participants, and study personnel involved in treatment administration, patient care, and outcome assessment were masked to treatment allocation throughout the study. Treatments were delivered as a once-only rectal enema. The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants with a reduction of 75 points or more in IBS-SSS score at 90 days after treatment compared with baseline, assessed in all patients who received their allocated treatment. All participants were advised to report any adverse event during follow-up to their study contact, preferably by telephone. A patient representative was involved in the planning of the trial. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04691544).

Findings

Between May 5, 2021, and July 14, 2022, we assessed 2304 individuals for eligibility, and 450 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned to the intervention group (299) or placebo group (151); two randomly assigned participants were excluded from analyses because their allocated treatments were switched. 293 (65%) of 448 participants were women, 155 (35%) were men, and the median age was 36 years (IQR 29-44). 119 (40%) participants in the donor faecal microbiota transplantation group and 57 (38%) in the placebo group showed an improvement of at least 75 points on the IBS-SSS at 90 days after treatment. The absolute difference was 1·9 percentage points (95% CI -8·1 to 12·0; p=0·76). The proportion of participants with adverse events was similar in the two study groups.

Interpretation

The trial did not show a clinical benefit of faecal microbiota transplantation in patients with IBS. These findings suggest that microbiota modulation alone might be insufficient for symptom improvement in IBS.

KLINBEFORSK.
title: Faecal microbiota transplantation in irritable bowel syndrome (REFIT2): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

authors: Behrendt CA, Norgren L, Nicolajsen CW, Powell JT, Chuter V, Gupta PC, Woo K, Nordanstig J.
summary: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is the primary driver of premature death in global populations in recent decades. Mortality statistics, most publications, and guidelines in the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease field have traditionally focused on cardiac and cerebrovascular adverse events and causes of death. However, given the increasing prevalence of lower extremity peripheral arterial disease and its expanding burden on global health systems, such an emphasis might represent a skewed perception of vascular risk within the broader atherosclerotic spectrum. Although common risk factors appear similar in all atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease subgroups, several crucial differences exist, including pathophysiological details and lesion patterns, as well as adherence to guideline-based recommendations. Individuals with peripheral arterial disease frequently remain asymptomatic for many years, often decades, and are typically diagnosed only at an advanced stage of the condition. By this time, however, the expected long-term outcomes are already extremely poor. When diagnosed at this point, the overall 5-year mortality is between 30% and 50%, thus even surpassing outcomes of severe cancer and acute myocardial infarction. Compared with cardiac and cerebrovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease receives lower priority in research and clinical practice, which is compounded by poor patient adherence to preventive care, lifestyle modification, and pharmacological therapy. This clinical Series of three papers aims to improve this distressing situation. For this purpose, it is important to recognise the underacknowledgment, underdiagnosis, and undertreatment of peripheral arterial disease and to understand the complex inter-relationships behind it before suitable interdisciplinary measures can be initiated. In this Series paper, we want to reach the broad interdisciplinary community, and above all, those who see these patients every day in general practice and internal medicine. The focus is primarily on the global importance of peripheral atherosclerosis and its drivers. In paper 2 of this Series, readers are introduced to modern complementary therapy, ranging from the optimisation of risk factors and optimal pharmacological therapies to innovative endovascular procedures and traditional surgical treatments. In the sense of integrated care and a stepwise approach, the described therapy alternatives can be combined individually for each patient. Paper 3 of this Series provides readers with a deep insight into the global significance and burden of peripheral arterial disease. Since this disease is primarily characterised by its long-term, chronically progressive course, improving long-term outcomes represents a central aspect of this paper. It aims to further illuminate striking disparities between geographical regions, sexes, and socioeconomic groups. With strong recommendations, this clinical Series can help to guide both clinicians and policy makers towards effective preventive measures.
title: Understanding peripheral arterial disease in the current era.

authors: Tulamo R, Bradbury A, Hicks CW, Gottsäter A, Gupta PC, Rother U, Sigvant B, Hinchliffe R.
summary: People with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) of the lower limbs are at very high risk of cardiovascular events and therefore the cornerstone of their management is medical therapy and behaviour modification to reduce that risk. The risk of limb loss (through major amputation) is low in people with asymptomatic PAD or intermittent claudication with only a few patients progressing to the most severe form of PAD: chronic limb threatening ischaemia. Supervised exercise therapy is effective in patients with intermittent claudication to improve their walking capacity and avoids the risks associated with revascularisation procedures to improve blood flow to the limb. Although some people with intermittent claudication might need revascularisation, it is overused in this group. Revascularisation of stenosed or occluded arteries can be done by open or endovascular surgery and is generally reserved for people with chronic limb threatening ischaemia who are at highest risk of limb loss because these interventions carry substantial peri-procedural risks and often have minimal durability. Innovative therapies to treat PAD focus on improving health-related quality of life, reducing limb loss, and improving survival but the disease remains challenging due to its impact on multiple arterial levels and in different organ systems (polyvascular disease).
title: Current advancements in the care of peripheral arterial disease: modern approaches to medical, endovascular, and surgical treatment.

authors: Golledge J, Søgaard M, Svensson M, Gupta PC, Nikol S, Reis PEO, Mahlmann A, Fowkes FGR.
summary: This is the third paper in the peripheral arterial disease (PAD) Series. The first and second papers in this Series outline that PAD affects over 300 million people worldwide and can be diagnosed by non-invasive tests, as well as that treatment requires medications to reduce modifiable risk factors and that exercise therapy and revascularisation are required in selected patients. In this paper, the devastating effects of PAD at the individual level are described, including chronic pain, functional limitation, loss of independence, impaired physical and mental quality of life, unemployment, and financial instability. Individuals with PAD are also at high risk of major adverse events, including major amputation, myocardial infarction, stroke, and death. The burden of PAD falls heavily on underserved groups, including women, First Nations Peoples globally, other non-White individuals, patients with financial insecurities, and those living in remote areas. Recommendations to advance PAD management are presented and include short-term changes, such as improving disease awareness and introducing multidisciplinary models of care that deliver more holistic medical and rehabilitation care, as well as long-term changes, such as testing whether screening and initiation of early medical management can reduce the burden of PAD. Furthermore, modification of health-care services is needed to provide better access for underserved, rural and remote, First Nations, and low-income populations.
title: Peripheral arterial disease: adverse impacts, disparities in outcomes, and the path ahead.

authors: Fancourt D, Bradt J, Fietje N, Tan MKB, Campbell D, Ibanez A, Sonke J, Patel V, Abdulla S, Mak HW, Sajnani N.
summary: Despite arts engagement being a ubiquitous human behaviour across human history, research and awareness on the health benefits of engagement are still emerging, accelerating over the past decade. Building on the evidence and research challenges outlined in the first paper of this Lancet collection, this Review puts forward a series of roadmaps for advancing research, policy, and practice to enable appropriate and effective integration of the arts into health and wellbeing systems globally. First and foremost, we advocate for the fundamental principle that all individuals, regardless of their characteristics and location, should have regular opportunities to engage in the arts, proposing policy and research steps to monitor and achieve this goal. Second, we emphasise the importance of implementing population-level strategies that use the arts as part of broader portfolios of approaches to help address the fundamental determinants of health inequities. Third, we underscore the necessity of developing and embedding across society diverse public-health pathways that connect individuals living with or at risk of health challenges to the arts within communities. Fourth, we argue for more clinical innovation in integrating bespoke evidence-based arts and creative arts therapies programmes into clinical care across the care pathway. Finally, we stress the crucial need for enhanced cross-sectoral stakeholder engagement and more strategic investment and research to facilitate the development and dissemination of the necessary tools, training, and evidence to achieve these objectives.
title: Developing roadmaps for advancing practice, research, and policy in the arts and health.
